# Fox, goose and beans (goose-fox-beans): Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script (pilot)

**Runnable.** `goose-fox-beans.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.34) and `goose-fox-beans-rules.soar` (16 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`). Needs Soar 9.6.6 or a 9.6.50 build.

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . goose-fox-beans.soar --seed 1 --cap 100000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . goose-fox-beans.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_plan.py goose-fox-beans init-fox.world

## Results (Soar 9.6.50, library v2.34, 16 Nov 2026)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Example states | init-fox: goal false, failure false; fail-fox and fail-fox2: failure true; final-fox: goal true |
| Seeds 1-3, library defaults | solved; 11 / 7 / 25 crossings (7 is the shortest); 6,097 / 3,437 / 16,517 decisions; seed 1 takes 3.4 s |
| Independent replay (`check_plan.py`) | every crossing legal, no losing state reached, goal holds (all three seeds) |
| Settings probe (P6, `probe.json`) | operator: 43 crossings over 3 seeds, 26,051 decisions; tie-impasse: 67, 10,273. Kept the library defaults |
| Cost options, for information (`probe-cost.json`; the English does not ask for the shortest plan, so they are not used) | operator + unit cost + optimize: 43 / 7 / 19 crossings; tie-impasse + unit cost + optimize: 23 / 7 / 11 |

The plans are safe but often not the shortest, even with `^optimize true`. The agent moves a block over and straight back: nothing in the instructions forbids returning to an earlier situation, and the library's look-ahead takes any move that still reaches the goal within the current depth. This is a library question (shortest plans when the task gives no repeated-state rule), not a translation error; it matches the open item on artists-and-managers.

## Assumption ledger

| ID | Statement | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| A-F1 | 5 | "the boat and a block": the block is not the boat. |
| A-F2 | 5 | Both the boat and the block move to the opposite bank. |
| A-F3 | 18 | "all the blocks" includes the boat, which is a block in the world file (category block, shape boat); final-fox has the boat on the destination bank. |
| A-F4 | 18 | "all the blocks" is expanded over the four blocks of the world file, so the goal test is positive. |
| A-F5 | 8 | The second action has no name in the dialog; it is called `cross`. |
| A-F6 | 10, 13 | "on an opposite bank ... on the opposite bank": both blocks on the same bank. |

Convention notes: `opposite` is a maintained one-argument relation (it tests absence and decides legality); `current` is expanded in place; the losing conditions mark the state with `^failure <desireds>` (workbook GOL-015, W-LAH-011), which look-ahead returns as a failure evaluation.
